subject: [PATCH v6 12/19] selftests/mm: parameterize the mixed-source collapse case by source order

2026-09-19.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mixed-source collapse case in the selftests/mm test suite by introducing a new parameter to specify the source order alongside the target order. The source order is used when collapsing contpte-mapped sources into larger mTHP, and the patch adds checks to ensure that the source order is supported and not below the target order. This change allows for more flexible testing of memory management scenarios.

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: Approved the patch with a Reviewed-by and Tested-by tag. The code looks good to them.
reviews.raw_body:
On 9/19/26 8:24 AM, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>
> 
> collapse_order_mixed_sources() faults its region as order-2 folios and
> collapses them to the -c target.  Order 2 is below the contpte size on
> every arm64 page size, so nothing in this suite collapses a contpte-mapped
> source on purpose.
> 
> Let -s name the source order alongside -c.  The case then faults at that
> order, keeping order 2 when -s is absent, and the source order has to be a
> supported mTHP order below the target.  The other mTHP cases are
> unaffected: mthp_push_target_order() enables only the target order.
> 
> A -c at or below -s is refused before any case runs: the sources would
> already be the size being asked for.  Without the check the generic cases
> fail on that one by one instead of saying why.
> 
> "-s 5 -c 7" on arm64/64K then collapses contpte-mapped sources into a
> larger mTHP.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Acked-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>
> Tested-by: Muhammad Usama Anjum <usama.anjum@arm.com>
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---

LGTM.
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
Tested-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>

2026-09-23.patch_summary: This patch series introduces parameterization of the mixed-source collapse case by source order in selftests/mm. The goal is to allow for more flexible testing and reduce test failures due to unsupported source orders.
